runTopic: reviewed visual evidence integrity and fail-closed scoring semantics

substantiveCommits.message: qa: add reviewed visual evidence integrity contract
qa: reject ambiguous reviewed visual evidence
qa: bind reviewed evidence integrity to visual gate

problemFound.summary: The canonical gate configuration was already locked, but the manually reviewed evidence arrays were not separately required to be exact sets. The numeric evaluator consumes categories, critical-defect reviews and captures by ID lookup, so duplicate or unknown entries were an avoidable ambiguity. Category correctiveAction text was also present in the schema but not fail-closed for scoring.
risk: ambiguous duplicate capture/category/critical-defect entries in reviewed evidence
unknown extra entries surviving manual authoring
deductions recorded without a concrete corrective action
incomplete observed-reference bookkeeping being mistaken for a complete manual review

implementation.integration: QualityBlockVisualGateIntegrityQA now validates the reviewed-evidence integrity contract in every source-side gate integrity pass and validates the completed reviewed evidence before enabling the normal evidence-bound scoring menu.
rules: exactly hero, oblique and grazing capture entries; duplicate/unknown view IDs fail
exactly nine canonical category entries; duplicate/unknown category IDs fail
exactly twelve canonical critical-defect reviews; duplicate/unknown defect IDs fail
each category requires observed evidence text and non-empty correctiveAction text
any category below full weight requires explicit deduction rationale
each category and critical-defect review requires at least one observed view/crop/temporal reference
reviewed evidence requires renderVerified=true and native 3840x2160 capture declarations
the new validator awards zero Visual Fidelity points

qualityState.expectedVisualScoreImpact: 0 direct points. This change prevents false or ambiguous scoring and forces each deducted category to carry an actionable correction before PASS can be considered from real rendered evidence.
